title: Patient Payment Plans and the Unrelieved Laboratory Burden: Patient Financial Assistance Program Renewal Rule
content:
**Clause.** For a renewal application under the Patient Financial Assistance Program, balances carried on a Patient Payment Plans plan are treated as follows: a household whose payment plan is active with no installment recorded missed within the last 6 months takes every installment it has paid on the plan out of the burden; a household whose payment plan is defaulted adds to the burden every returned-payment fee posted on its invoices; any other household's burden is neither reduced nor increased for a plan.

"Within the last 6 months" takes the missed-installment entries dated fewer than 6 whole calendar months before today.

| Plan status in Patient Payment Plans | Installment recorded missed within the last 6 months | Effect on the unrelieved laboratory burden |
|---|---|---|
| Active | No | Every installment paid on the plan is taken out |
| Active | Yes | Neither reduced nor increased |
| Defaulted | Not read | Every returned-payment fee posted on the household's invoices is added |
| Pending acceptance, past due, paid off or cancelled | Not read | Neither reduced nor increased |
| No plan | Not applicable | Neither reduced nor increased |

## Worked figures (hypothetical households; today 15 September 2026)

- Active plan; installments of $85.00 paid on it in each of seven months; the only missed installment was recorded on 10 January 2026, 8 whole months ago. No installment was missed within the last 6 months, so $595.00, every installment paid on the plan, is taken out of the burden.
- Same plan, but an installment recorded missed on 10 June 2026, 3 whole months ago: the burden is neither reduced nor increased.
- Defaulted plan; two returned-payment fees of $25.00 each posted on the household's invoices: $50.00 is added to the burden.
